Mercaptans (thiols) and organic sulfides contain sulfur atoms that can be reduced by strong reducing agents. When these compounds react with strong reducing agents, several hazardous outcomes are possible:

1. Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) gas can be generated, which is highly toxic. Strong reducing agents can reduce the sulfur in mercaptans and sulfides to form H₂S gas.

2. Some of these reactions can be exothermic (generating heat).

3. Depending on the specific compounds and conditions, flammable gases might also be produced.

The most significant hazard when strong reducing agents react with mercaptans/organic sulfides is the production of hydrogen sulfide gas, which is extremely toxic even at low concentrations. H₂S is a colorless gas with a characteristic "rotten egg" odor that can cause respiratory paralysis and death at high concentrations.
